why: Pier Road roundabout (Western Way, London Road, Water Street, Pier Road): a small structure mapped on its island stops the roundabout being found, so the scene had a loop of one-way roads the route planner would not drive.

Waterloo roundabout: London Road's way in from the east is a short unnamed piece (32 m), which the route planner will not turn on to, so the roundabout could not be driven westbound. Named as the road it carries.

Water Street at the Pier Road roundabout: the way between the ring and this node (an unmarked crossing) was 9.6 m long, too short for the lane path, so the car's line cut the corner on to the pavement leaving the roundabout. The node moved 8.5 m south along Water Street (no change of shape), so that piece is 18 m.
